messages:
maya: Heads-up — I hit a weird auth bleed when using the new CredentialProviderFactory + async clients.
maya: Repro is two clients instantiated with different API keys; after the first key rotates, some requests from the second client start failing with 401.
samir: ah interesting. can you paste a minimal repro?
maya: gist of it below. this happens in an asyncio app with concurrent tasks.
maya: ```py
from redwood import Client, CredentialProviderFactory

factory = CredentialProviderFactory()
# factory.register_from_env()  # we use explicit keys in this repro

client_a = Client(credential_provider=factory.for_key("AAAKEY"))
client_b = Client(credential_provider=factory.for_key("BBBKEY"))

# async tasks: sometimes client_b starts sending AAAKEY after a rotate()
async def worker(client):
    await client.generate("ping")

# simulate rotate on factory
factory.rotate("AAAKEY", "AAAKEY-NEW")
```
maya: Logs show client_b requests with Authorization: Bearer AAAKEY-NEW even though client_b was created with BBBKEY.
nate: that sounds like provider instances share mutable state somewhere (maybe a cached token or a global context).
samir: do you see this only when calling factory.rotate, or also when env var changes? any difference with sync vs async?
maya: only observed when calling factory.rotate. env var swap didn't reproduce. sync single-threaded apps are fine.
carla: can you try calling factory.for_key(...) and explicitly copying provider state? may be a pointer alias.
maya: quick workaround: passing api_key directly to Client(...) avoids it. but we need rotation support for long-lived clients.
samir: could you add the exact headers block from a failing request (redact keys)? that helps triage.
maya: sure — snippet:
maya: ```
> POST /v1/generate
> Authorization: Bearer BBBKEY    # expected
> X-Auth-Observed: AAAKEY-NEW    # actual header server logged
``` 
maya: server trace shows mismatch at the gateway level.
nate: assigning to eng-devex for investigation. sounds like a factory-level cache key is being reused.
carla: also worth checking any module-level singletons in credential provider implementation — common source of cross-client leaks.
samir: can you open a GH issue with the repro and tag @eng-devex + include a small dockerized repro? I'll triage.
maya: done: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4122
carla: thanks. adding a unit test for multi-client rotation scenarios should catch regressions.
devex-bot: Issue #4122 created and assigned to @nate. Priority: P2. ETA: investigating today. :robot_face:
maya: thanks all. filing this because it's causing intermittent auth failures in a customer integration (async worker pool). will follow up with traces.
samir: appreciated — if you can include a small recording of request headers sequence that would speed a fix. :thumbsup:
